summary.headline: Ganesh Benzoplast Q4 FY26 consol PAT swung to INR152 mn from a loss, but JNPT rental reset (~INR23 cr rise) compresses LST margins for 2-3 years.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR1,115 mn and PAT turned to INR152 mn from a INR132 mn loss in Q4 FY25. Full-year FY26 consol revenue grew 10% to INR4,114 mn and PAT rose 93% to INR733 mn, with EPS of INR10.19. Management attributed the margin dip to a 30-year JNPT lease rental reset, with the old plots' rental rising to about INR25 cr from about INR2 cr, partly offset by a one-time INR9 cr income. Expansion of about 50,000 kL at JNPT is under way, with management guiding to commissioning by calendar year-end 2026.

segments.name: LST (JNPT, Kochi, Goa terminals)
segments.commentary: JNPT running at about 100% utilisation, Kochi at 80-85%+, Goa close to zero after bunkering demand left post mining ban. Management said rental segment EBITDA margin was about 45-47%, unchanged, per an analyst's read of prior disclosures; the company did not restate the segment margin split this quarter.

segments.name: Chemical division
segments.commentary: Management said Q4 had two exceptional charges: recertification costs for UK/Europe and settlement of staff dues and salary hikes. Excluding these, Chemical PAT would have risen at least 15% YoY. Chemical capex is limited to small debottlenecking.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Large INR175 cr JSW port order; engineering complete, groundwork expected after monsoon. Margins described as higher single digit. Value executed not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: JNPT expansion of about 50,000 kL (about 40,000-49,000 kL phase) to be completed by December 2026 (calendar year-end), with revenue expected from Q4 FY26/calendar year-end.
A further about 60,000 kL capacity is planned for next year; combined capex for both phases is about INR100 cr. Installed capacity to rise about 15%.

Management expects rentals to rise 5-6% annually on existing tanks, and the EBITDA margin to recover over 2-3 years; another view was that the cost is recovered in 15-18 months with new tanks at about 80% EBITDA margin.
Goa petroleum modification (blended petrol approvals) to start after monsoon and finish by 31 March 2027; no contract signed yet. Capex about INR2 cr.
Chemical expected to remain on a steady path with no major capacity project.
capex_capacity: Total installed capacity about 3.50 lakh kL; about 2.80 lakh kL sits on JNPT plots, per management.
JNPT utilisation almost 100%, Goa close to zero, Kochi above 80-85%, overall about 95%.
JNPT expansion of about 50,000 kL under way at capex of INR40-50 cr for this phase; 3 large 45,000 kL tanks are being built.
Ammonia storage and LPG bullets capex of around INR450-500 cr is still under discussion and not initiated; about 5-6 acres of JNPT land is set aside.
Visakhapatnam LOI progress is on hold because of a dispute between a prior plot holder and the Visakhapatnam port.
demand_pricing: JNPT rentals are a mix of long-term storage contracts and spot. Management said no exceptional demand arose from the war-related supply disruption, so no pricing windfall was taken.

Management said JNPT lease rental reset happens every 30 years (last in 2025, next in 2055). The old plots' rental rose to about INR25 cr from about INR2 cr, a provision booked in Q4 for the cumulative amount.
A one-time exceptional income of INR9 cr came from termination of an LPG arrangement (around Feb-March 2025 per management).
Management said the company is pursuing a Singapore subsidiary for chemical basket trade, still at a preliminary stage.
Receivables over 6 months have risen because of extended credit terms in EPC; retention money is paid after one year. Management said there is no bad debt issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and why is Goa near zero?
qa_highlights.answer: JNPT is near 100%, Cochin 80-85%+, Goa close to zero since the bunkering business left after the Goa mining ban; overall about 95%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall because of rental expense?
qa_highlights.answer: The JNPT land was acquired in 1995, and the 30-year rental reset took effect in 2025. Old-plot rent rose to about INR25 cr from about INR2 cr.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Chemical slow in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no slowdown. Two exceptional items (UK/Europe recertification and staff dues/salary settlement) hit the quarter; excluding them, Chemical PAT would have risen at least 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consol EBITDA margin fall from about 21-22% in Q3 to about 18-19% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full INR25 cr annual lease rental was provisioned in Q4 cumulatively, and the YoY margin drop was about INR6 cr against the INR23 cr rise. The company expects to pass the cost to customers and recover it in 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 50% capex complete by Q1 or the full phase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entire 49,000 kL phase will be completed by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add ports outside JNPT, Kochi and Goa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will only deploy capital where ROI matches or beats JNPT. No such opportunity has been found, though it is open to overseas deals with back-to-back contracts.

risks_watch: JNPT rental reset compresses LST margin; recovery timeline of 2-3 years depends on 5-6% annual rental escalation.
Goa terminal near zero utilisation, with INR10-12 lakh/month holding cost; petroleum handling there has no signed contract.
Expansion timing: 50,000 kL due by December 2026 and 60,000 kL next year; any slip would delay revenue.
Receivables over 6 months rising because of EPC credit terms and retention money.
Visakhapatnam LOI on hold; ammonia/LPG bullet capex of INR450-500 cr not yet initiated.
Management could not give the JSW EPC executed value or the Goa total historical investment on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the JNPT expansion and long-term rental escalation, but defensive on margin compression and receivables. Several answers were vague or deferred (Goa investment, EPC progress, segment margin split), and some management statements conflicted on timing.
key_quotes: So, this is every 30 years, there is a reset in the rentals by the ports.
Chemical is also running more or less on steady state.
So, the combined capex for both of the capacities together is approximately INR100 crores.
